reasoning: Both are high quality. B wins narrowly: its outside-signal connections are cleaned up with the Vide scope, it makes number keys respect locks, its close button can take gamepad focus and it restores the previous selection, it draws a real padlock and a pressed state, and it keeps all of its UI inside the safe area. A has nicer scrolling, previews and hints, but leaves its connections unscoped and opts its backdrop out of the safe area. B's luau-lsp failure is a 'path does not exist' error for a file that is in its diff, so it most likely comes from the checker rather than from B's code.

criteria.criterion: Every action works with every input
criteria.note: Tiles, close, open and backdrop all use Activated; E/ButtonY toggle via CAS, ButtonB bound while open; the doc table covers touch, mouse/keyboard and controller and matches the code.

manageGamepadSelection sets GuiService.SelectedObject to the selected tile on open; the panel has SelectionGroup with Stop on all four sides; B closes. The close button is Selectable=false, so it can't be reached by gamepad.

TouchTarget is 56, the open button 84x104 sits right edge mid-height, and tiles are at least 104 wide under UIScale; the main gui uses CoreUISafeInsets, but the tap-to-close backdrop ScreenGui uses ScreenInsets.None.
Status shows '🔒 Level N' with a padlock over the preview; ×0 shows as a number; a locked press shows a 'X unlocks at Level N' footer message.

Name, count and lock are always on the tile; the green stroke and ✓ badge mark the selection; hover uses MouseEnter/MouseLeave, which can stick on touch; there is no distinct pressed state beyond focus scale.
Fixed TextSize of 17-32 under a UIScale that reaches 1.6 at 1080p, on a dark panel with white or light text; the emoji glyphs depend on the font.
Changed and BlockTypeChanged update sources and the UI is bound, but those connections in InventoryState.start are never cleaned up with the Vide scope.
All checks pass, BlockPlacer is untouched apart from setEnabled use, and the code is clean and modular.

criteria.criterion: Every action works with every input
criteria.note: Tiles, close, backdrop and the HUD button use Activated; the B key and ButtonY toggle, ButtonB is bound at High priority while open; the doc tables match the code.

focusTile sets GuiService.SelectedObject via the tile's action on open; the panel has SelectionGroup with Stop; ButtonB closes; the close button is selectable; the previous selection is restored on close.
88 px HUD button right edge mid-height on phones, close button 44-52, tiles 96-104, CoreUISafeInsets; fitScale can shrink the panel to 0.5, putting tiles near 48.
Drawn LockIcon plus 'Level N' text, x0 shown, a locked press shakes the tile and sets the status line to 'Ice unlocks at level 4'.
Everything is visible on the tile; pressed scale of 0.94, a focus ring, and a 'Using' pill plus gold stroke; hover is tracked through MouseMovement only.
Fixed TextSizes from Theme (Name 20, Count 18, Caption 16) on a mostly opaque panel; compact captions are a bit small.
cleanup(BlockInventory.Changed:Connect(...)) and cleanup(BlockTypeChanged...) in the app scope; entries/level/selectedName are sources rendered through indexes and show.

The luau-lsp failure is a path-resolution error that looks like tooling, not a type error; the BlockPlacer change to skip locked blocks is reasonable; uses const and @game string requires; part of the diff was truncated.

strengths: Locked message in the footer, Reduced Motion support, open button doubles as a current-block display
weaknesses: Outside-signal connections are not tied to the Vide scope
Backdrop ScreenGui opts out of the safe area with ScreenInsets.None
Close button can't take gamepad focus; number keys can still pick locked blocks (documented)

Fixes number keys to respect locks

Restores focus on close and hides touch controls while open
Detailed design note with playtest questions
